item.description:
A maintenance release: more accurate, better-disclosed usage analytics, and one search fix.

Changed

  • Usage analytics now run on swift-stats 0.3.0. Install figures carry straight across the upgrade (no drop, no spike of "new" installs): Herald already counted installs with a random per-install identifier.
  • Usage reports are more accurate, and cover a few more features. Herald now reports which settings are changed (never what they were changed to, or for which domain), when a label is added or removed (never which label), when a new-mail banner is clicked, and whether macOS allowed notifications after you turned them on. Actions record where they were triggered from (toolbar, keyboard, menu…), a search is counted once per Return, and a compose window that closes leaving a draft is counted once. As before, nothing you type, no names, addresses or identifiers of your mail or accounts, and no exact counts are ever sent.
  • Settings › Privacy and the README now list everything each report carries: the Herald version and build, macOS version, Mac model (never your Mac's name), processor type, and your language and region settings, alongside which features are used.
  • The privacy manifest now declares the per-install identifier as Device ID (not linked to you, not used for tracking). Herald has always sent it; earlier builds just didn't declare it.
  • Development builds never send usage reports unless explicitly turned on.

Fixed

  • Automatic mail checks no longer count as using Herald. Herald used to report every background sync — every 15 seconds while it was in front — so a Mac left running with Herald open looked in use all night. Only syncs you start, the one at launch, and the moment sync stops working are reported now.
  • A launch is counted once, not once per account, and not at all when Herald starts behind other apps.
  • Launching Herald straight into the foreground now starts its analytics session properly (it previously had no "app opened" event), and quitting makes a best-effort attempt to send anything still queued.
  • Pressing Return in the search field right after typing now searches what you typed, not the text from a quarter-second earlier.
